definitions.explanation: A family unit consisting of parents and their children only, without extended family members such as grandparents. A sociological term that has become common in everyday Japanese.

examples.japanese: {核家族|かくかぞく}が{増|ふ}えている。
うちは{核家族|かくかぞく}で、{祖父母|そふぼ}は{別|べつ}に{暮|く}らしている。
examples.english: Our family is a nuclear family; our grandparents live separately.

examples.japanese: {核家族|かくかぞく}{化|か}が{進|すす}んだことで、{育児|いくじ}の{負担|ふたん}が{親|おや}に{集中|しゅうちゅう}するようになった。
examples.english: As nuclear families became more common, the burden of childcare became concentrated on the parents.

notes:
USAGE:
{核家族|かくかぞく} is contrasted with {大家族|だいかぞく} (extended family) or {三世代同居|さんせだいどうきょ} (three generations living together). The trend toward {核家族|かくかぞく} has been a major social change in postwar Japan.

COMPOUNDS:
- {核家族|かくかぞく}{化|か}: the trend toward nuclear families
- {核家族|かくかぞく}{世帯|せたい}: nuclear family household

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大家族|だいかぞく}: large/extended family
